ipni_publication.name: Anthriscus Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Although purporting to be ed. 16 of Linnaeus' Systema vegetabilium, this work must be attributed to Sprengel. Editio decima sexta, curante Curtio Sprengel ... volumen v. sistens indicem generum, specierum et synonymorun, auctore Antonio Sprengel ...Sprengel (preface v) acknowledged contributions from several people, viz., ‘Accedit Willdenowii herbarium, cuius usque inspiciendi copiam fecit magistratus, faciunt amici. Super haec et celebranda benevolentia exterorum, maxime R. Brownii, Smithii, Balbisii, Delilii, Gussonii, Vivianii, Besseri aliorumque, qui et plantas rarissimas largiti sunt et libros praestantissimos.’ For all the new combinations or new names ascribed to the preceding authors, they are the authors. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

Some confusion has arisen over edition numbers since TL-2 No. 4769 for Species Plantarum has ed. 4 as a Reichard edition. Although the latter is entitled Systema Plantarum ... editio novissima it includes Species Plantarum and other works, and TL-2 states that it can be counted as the 4th edition of Species Plantarum. Editio decima sexta, curante Curtio Sprengel ... volumen v. sistens indicem generum, specierum et synonymorun, auctore Antonio Sprengel ...Sprengel (preface v) acknowledged contributions from several people, viz., ‘Accedit Willdenowii herbarium, cuius usque inspiciendi copiam fecit magistratus, faciunt amici. Super haec et celebranda benevolentia exterorum, maxime R. Brownii, Smithii, Balbisii, Delilii, Gussonii, Vivianii, Besseri aliorumque, qui et plantas rarissimas largiti sunt et libros praestantissimos.’ For all the new combinations or new names ascribed to the preceding authors, they are the authors. ipni_publication.name: Anthriscus Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Cynanchum laeve Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Ficus macrophylla Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Hedeoma Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Phyllanthus amarus Schumach. & Thonn.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Preprinted from: Dansk. Vid. Selsk. Skr. 3: 21-248. 1827; 4:1-236. 1829. History of dates of publication discussed in: Kew Bull. 1953(2): 280. 1953. Specific names followed by diagnoses and descriptions signed S. must be ascribed to Schumacher, those followed by Th. to Thonning; many names are followed by a diagnosis signed S. and a description signed Th. It seems reasonable to attribute these to Schumacher in accordance with the botanical custom of the time although joint authorship can also be defended. Unsigned names or diagnoses should be attributed to Schumacher. The title-page gives Schumacher as the author; Thonning's name appears only as collector. (vide TL-2, #11.360). ipni_publication.name: Pycnanthemum muticum (Michx.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Sabal minor (Jacq.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]

ipni_publication.name: Tephrosia virginiana (L.) Pers.
ipni_publication.publication_remarks: Persoon (vol. 1: preface x, paragraph 3) mentioned: Varietates praecipuae et subspecies non omissae sunt. Speciebus obscuris, aut quoad sedem dubiis, rel accuratiori indagationi subjiciendis, signa crucis seu astericsum apposui. Boivin (in Brittonia 14: 330. 1962) interpreted that * sign refers to the rank subspecies and Greek letters refer to varieties. Greuter (in Candollea 23: 90-92. 1968) concluded that the Greek lettered taxa, unless indicated as variety, are unranked and * sign refers to obscurely known species. Persoon treated most of his infrageneric names at the rank of subgenus (vide preface ix, paragraph 2 (Melius autem judicavi, eas species (nonnullis forte tamen excipiendis) ab aliis leviter in charactere aberrantes, imprimis si genus minus amplum sit, sub divisione peculiari aut subgenere, quo etiam nonnula Botanicorum recentium genera relata sunt, comprehendere, ne ultra necessitatem genera multiplicentur) and index title in vol. 1, p. 527 (Index Generum, subgenerum, nominum Familiae plantarum et synonymorum generum praecipuorum)). [See George K. Brizicky, Taxon 18(4): 646, 649. 1969]. Occasionally, Persoon used parenthetical epithets (e.g., 1: 411: ‘Combretum decandrum (album))’; he (preface p. ix) explained his usage as: ‘in parenthesi nomen quasi secundarium passim addidi, quo idea plantae forte distinctior concipi possit’. It is evident that Persoon proposed C. album and such names as alternative names. [BHL_title_id:638] [BHL_page_id:33189654]
